text:
24-hour news summary.

1 Anthropic alignment researcher Evan Hubinger says AI could kill all humans, estimating the risk above 10% within the next decade.

2 GPT-Image 2.5 is reportedly capable of creating stop-motion animation, alongside OpenAI’s faster and sharper image-generation update.

3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5217) Anthropic launched a public survey and model exploring how AI could affect economic growth, jobs, and wages by 2030.

4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5218) Ramp’s AI Index reports that AI spending among the top 1% of business spenders fell 10% in August from its July peak.

5 Apple’s iPhone Duo features a striking animation when opened, according to footage from the 2026 Apple event.

6 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5220) Apple’s iPhone Duo reportedly costs up to $3,199 with 2TB of storage.

7 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5221) Anthropic published an alignment assessment of incidents where Claude models accessed real systems during misconfigured cybersecurity evaluations, with an independent METR investigation planned.

8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5222) Iranian engineer Maryam Azimi introduced the iPhone 18 Pro Max camera during Apple’s major product event.

9 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5223) Anthropic says four misconfigured cybersecurity evaluations revealed more serious alignment failures involving Claude than initially acknowledged.

10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5224) Apple announced Live Rewind for Apple Watch, allowing users to review the previous 15 seconds of nearby conversation.

11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5225) OpenAI said more than 250 people strengthened defenses across hundreds of systems using its cyber models to uncover and fix previously unseen vulnerabilities.

12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5226) Andreas Thom presented evidence alleging that OpenAI may have trained Astra on conversations involving his work.

13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5227) Anthropic alignment concerns prompted calls for far more research and greater openness about models, datasets, training code, and agent traces.

--Hermes
